name: Aristocratic Upbringing
description: Your formative environment exposed you to the customs, education, and social expectations of aristocratic households or communities. This Upbringing may reflect being raised among nobles, household attendants, tutors, or others familiar with such customs. It is available to any Species and does not require noble birth, a title, personal wealth, a royal court, servants, or a particular later Background.

benefits.name: Household or Community Language
benefits.description: Learn one language used in the household or aristocratic social environment that shaped your upbringing. Common is an appropriate choice where it was spoken there. This learned language is separate from Species traits and any language gained through a later Background.

benefits.name: Aristocratic Skill
benefits.description: Choose one Skill reflecting the education and experience of your formative aristocratic environment: History, Insight, Persuasion, Deception, or Performance.

benefits.name: Aristocratic Competency
benefits.description: Choose exactly one training benefit: one particular type of gaming set, or the native Calligraphy, Painting, or Cooking Competency. These choices reflect practices learned in your formative community and do not include equipment ownership or several unrelated training benefits.
Choose proficiency with one particular type of gaming set; do not gain every gaming set type.
Gain training in the native Calligraphy Competency, associated with Calligrapher's Supplies. The equipment association grants neither ownership nor a second equipment proficiency.
Gain training in the native Painting Competency, associated with Painter's Supplies. The equipment association grants neither ownership nor a second equipment proficiency.
Gain training in the native Cooking Competency, associated with Cook's Utensils. The equipment association grants neither ownership nor a second equipment proficiency.

benefits.name: Aristocratic Protocol
benefits.description: When dealing with aristocratic communities whose customs you know, you understand their ordinary titles, ranks, forms of address, etiquette, and customary ways to seek introductions or an audience. You can recall that familiar ordinary protocol without a check required solely to remember it. Customs that are unfamiliar, deliberately concealed, unusual, or uncertain may require inquiry or ordinary adjudication by the GM. Knowing the appropriate protocol does not guarantee admission, an audience, favorable treatment, a title, authority, wealth, property, influence over others, or recognition as a noble.

reviewNotes: Approved independent Aristocratic Upbringing, representing formative exposure to aristocratic household and community practices; a character does not need noble parents, personal status, wealth, or the Noble Background.
One learned language used in the formative household or social setting; Common is eligible when used there, but not automatically required or inherited from Species.

Provisional initial balance baseline approved by owner after corpus review: choose exactly one Skill from History, Insight, Persuasion, Deception, or Performance, plus one training benefit from a specific Gaming Set equipment proficiency or Calligraphy, Painting, or Cooking Competency. Counts may be revisited in a broader balance pass.

The mixed proficiency choice uses one outer benefit-choice with four alternatives. Choosing a gaming set triggers one nested gaming-set category selection; choosing Calligraphy, Painting, or Cooking grants only that existing Competency.

Calligraphy, Painting, and Cooking are native Competencies with independently represented ranks and proficiency; the Gaming Set alternative is a distinct, binary equipment proficiency. Associated tools do not create extra training grants. Review the alternative outcomes together for balance.

Aristocratic Protocol grants reliable knowledge of ordinary protocol in aristocratic settings familiar to the character without an ordinary check solely to recall it. Unknown, secret, or foreign customs remain subject to normal adjudication.
Aristocratic Protocol does not grant social admission, authority, noble status, an audience, property, wealth, or the Noble Background's Position of Privilege.
No Upbringing startingEquipment package, fixed ability increases, Origin feat, household servants, instrument or kit items, or additional Background grants are provided.

Aristocratic Upbringing and Noble Background may be selected together without implying one from the other. Overlapping Skills, languages, or Gaming Set training await the single corpus-wide duplicate-grant policy.
Native mixed-benefit choice execution, Skill/Competency and language projection, parent/default selection, and cross-Species combinations remain deferred to common implementation.
The chosen Calligraphy, Painting, or Cooking Competency grants proficiency and no ranks. The Gaming Set alternative grants only its selected equipment qualification.
